candidate_history.answer:
**Short answer:** Weave can call your endpoint only after remote scoring is enabled for your organization and your endpoint's host is on the allowlist. Scoring starts after the turn ends, so it isn't a step that produces the answer. The docs I read don't say exactly when the user receives the answer.

## Compact setup outline

1. **Trace the agent (Python).**
   - Call `weave.init()`.
   - Open a conversation with `start_conversation`.
   - Open each exchange with `start_turn`.
   - Wrap model calls in `start_llm` and tool executions in `start_tool` [S4].
   - The quickstart shows these nested in a multi-turn loop. They appear in the **Agents** view [S9].
   - Use the **Conversations** tab to inspect them [S4].

2. **Rerun regression questions.**
   - Keep a fixed task list. Run each task inside `EvaluationLogger.log_prediction(...)`, with the agent run inside it [S10].
   - After a change, rerun the same tasks with `EvaluationLogger` using a new `model` label, such as `"v2"` [S11].
   - Use Weave's evaluation comparison to see improvements or regressions [S11].
   - The tutorial's scorer is an LLM judge. For the same flow, you could write your own scorer function instead, because the tutorial says Weave doesn't prescribe the scorer's shape [S10].

3. **Score live turns with your HTTP endpoint.** Use a remote scorer signal.
   - Publish a `RemoteScorer`.
   - Activate a `Monitor` with `scorers=[scorer]` and `op_names=["weave.genai.turn_ended"]` [S7].
   - Alternatively, create it in the UI: **Agents → Signals → New signal → Remote scorer** [S8-UI details are on the same page as S1; I did not read that section in full].
   - Results appear as tags or ratings on the **Signals** tab [S3].

## Prerequisites before Weave can call your endpoint (multi-tenant cloud)

- **Org setting.** Remote scoring is off by default. An organization or billing admin must turn on **Enable remote scoring** in the **Remote scoring** tab of the organization settings [S2].
- **Allowed hosts.** The admin must add at least one host under **Allowed hosts**. Saving with remote scoring enabled requires one [S2].
  - The worker checks the endpoint URL against the allowlist. It does the same for an OAuth token URL if you use OAuth [S2].
  - Wildcards must look like `*.corp.example.com`, and they don't match the bare domain [S2].
- **Endpoint rules.**
  - The endpoint must use HTTPS unless the deployment permits insecure HTTP.
  - It can't be a loopback, private, internal, or cloud-metadata address.
  - Redirects aren't followed [S2].
- **Authentication.** Choose `static_bearer` or `oauth_client_credentials` [S6].
  - Store the token or client secret in the secret store of the team that owns the project before you register the scorer.
  - The scorer configuration holds only the secret name [S6].
- **Response format.** Agent turn scoring requires the structured result format. Weave stores the tags and ratings as typed feedback columns [S1].

## Does scoring finish before the user gets the answer?

The documented sequence is:
1. A turn ends when its root span ends, and Weave emits `weave.genai.turn_ended`.
2. A separate agent scoring worker loads the matching signals.
3. The worker sends the `POST` and writes the result as feedback on the turn [S1].

So scoring is triggered by a completed turn and runs in a worker, not inside your agent's response code.

The retry rules show that it can take a while. The worker retries failed attempts up to three times within 30 seconds of the first attempt. A timeout uses the whole 30 seconds [S1].

I did not find a passage that states the exact moment the user receives the answer. In my searches I also found no feature that lets a remote scorer block or modify the response. Don't use this scorer as a pre-delivery policy gate. For that, you would need to call your own check in the agent code.

**Next step:** Ask your org admin to enable remote scoring and add your scorer's host. Then create the signal and test it on one conversation.

candidate_history.answer:
**Short answer:** Weave can't call your endpoint until remote scoring is enabled for your organization and your endpoint's host is on the allowlist. The docs I read describe scoring as a separate step that starts after a turn ends. They don't state the timing relative to the user's reply, so I can't promise that the reply doesn't wait on scoring.

**Compact setup outline**

1. **Trace the agent (conversations and tool calls).**
   - Install `weave` and call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` first. The agent tracing functions silently do nothing without it [S8].
   - Instrument with `start_conversation()`, `start_turn()`, `start_llm()` and `start_tool()`. Each can be used as a context manager or closed with `.end()` [S8][S9].
   - Traces appear in the **Agents** tab. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage and feedback [S3].

2. **Rerun regression questions.**
   - The agent-evaluation tutorial uses `weave.EvaluationLogger` with a `dataset` name and a `model` label for the agent version. After a change, you rerun the same tasks with a new label such as `"v2"` [S10].
   - You can then use Weave's compare-evaluations feature to see whether the new version improved or regressed [S10].
   - The tutorial also shows multi-turn rows. A row holds the prior conversation history plus the next user message [S4]. I only read part of that tutorial, so check it for the full loop.

3. **Send completed turns to your endpoint.**
   - Build the HTTP endpoint and register it as a `RemoteScorer`.
   - Then activate a `Monitor` whose `op_names` is `["weave.genai.turn_ended"]`. The same page shows this setup in the Weave UI under Agents > Signals > New signal > Remote scorer [S7].
   - Results appear as tags or ratings on the **Signals** tab [S1].

**Prerequisites before Weave can call the endpoint (multi-tenant Cloud)**

- **Remote scoring is off by default.** An organization or billing admin must open the organization's settings in Forge and go to the **Remote scoring** tab. They turn on **Enable remote scoring**, add at least one host under **Allowed hosts**, and save [S5].
- **Your host must be allowed.**
  - The scoring worker checks the endpoint URL, and the OAuth token URL if you use OAuth, against the allowlist [S5].
  - The URL must use HTTPS. Redirects aren't followed. Loopback, private, internal and cloud-metadata addresses are rejected [S5].
- **Credentials must be stored first.**
  - Weave authenticates with a bearer token, either `static_bearer` or `oauth_client_credentials`.
  - You store the token or client secret in the project team's secret store before registering the scorer. The scorer config holds only the secret name [S6].
- **The endpoint must return the structured result format.** Agent-turn scoring requires it, because tags and ratings are stored as typed feedback columns [S2]. I didn't read the request and response schema sections, so check those before building the endpoint.

**Does scoring finish before the user gets the answer?**

The docs don't say. They describe this sequence:
- A turn ends when its root span ends.
- That emits a `weave.genai.turn_ended` event.
- A separate agent scoring worker then loads the matching signals, sends the `POST` and writes the result as feedback [S2].

The scoring is therefore triggered by a completed turn and run by a worker. That is not a documented guarantee that it happens after your reply is delivered. Treat it as not part of your response path, and don't rely on the score being available when the user sees the answer. If this matters for your design, test it.

Endpoint timing:
- The worker makes up to three attempts within 30 seconds of the first attempt.
- It retries `5xx`, `408` and `429` responses.
- A timeout uses the whole 30 seconds and isn't retried.
- Other `4xx` responses aren't retried [S2].
- If your endpoint can't finish in time, return `503` quickly so Weave retries [S2].

**Next step:** Ask your org admin to enable remote scoring and allowlist your scorer host. Meanwhile, add the tracing instrumentation.

I didn't run any code, and I haven't verified the exact SDK signatures for the tracing functions.

candidate_history.answer:
Use three pieces: Agents tracing for inspection, `EvaluationLogger` for regression reruns, and a remote scorer signal for live scoring. A remote scorer must be enabled by an admin first. The docs I read don't say whether live scoring finishes before the user gets the answer.

**Setup outline**

1. **Inspect conversations and tool calls.** Call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]", ...)`. Then wrap your hand-written agent with `start_conversation`, `conv.start_turn`, `turn.start_llm` and `turn.start_tool` [S10]. The Agents view then shows each turn with its model call and tool calls nested inside [S10].
   - If you hand-instrument, the tutorial sets `settings={"implicitly_patch_integrations": False}`. Otherwise conversations can be traced twice [S10].
   - To record multi-turn history for testing, the tutorial seeds a fixed `conversation_history` and then sends the next user message [S4].

2. **Rerun regression questions.** The agent-evals tutorial uses `weave.EvaluationLogger(name=..., model="v2", dataset=...)`. You rerun the same tasks against the changed agent under a new `model` label [S9]. Weave's Compare evaluations then shows whether v2 improved or regressed against v1 on your logged scores, latency and cost [S9]. The tutorial scores with an LLM judge. I didn't verify here how to plug in your own scorer.

3. **Send completed answers to your endpoint.** Create a remote scorer signal in the UI (Agents → Signals → New signal → Remote scorer) or with the Python SDK [S2][S6]. A remote scorer signal is a `Monitor` whose `op_names` is `["weave.genai.turn_ended"]` [S1]. This is the Signals workflow for agents. Don't mix it with the legacy Calls and Monitors workflow [S2].

**Prerequisites before Weave can call your endpoint (multi-tenant cloud)**

- Remote scoring is off by default. An organization or billing admin must open `https://forge.coreweave.com/account-settings/[ORGANIZATION]/settings`, go to the **Remote scoring** tab and turn on **Enable remote scoring** [S6].
- The admin must add at least one entry under **Allowed hosts** for each host your scorer will call, then click **Save settings** [S6]. If you use OAuth, the token endpoint URL is checked against the same rules [S6].
- HTTPS is required. Redirects aren't followed. Loopback, private, internal and cloud-metadata addresses are rejected [S6].
- Store the bearer token or OAuth client secret in the project's team secret store before registering the scorer. The scorer config holds only the secret name [S7]. Weave authenticates to your endpoint with either `static_bearer` or `oauth_client_credentials` [S7].
- Your endpoint must return HTTP `200` with JSON `{"schema_version": 2, "result": ...}`. Each score `value` is a tag of at most 36 characters or a rating from 0.0 to 1.0 [S8]. Agent turn scoring requires this structured result format [S1].

**Does scoring finish before the user gets the answer?**

The docs don't say. They describe scoring as starting after a turn ends: when a root span ends, Weave emits `weave.genai.turn_ended`. A separate agent scoring worker then loads the matching signals, sends the `POST` and writes the result as feedback on the turn [S1]. I found no passage in the pages I read that says whether this runs before or after your agent returns the reply to the user. Don't rely on the score being available at response time, and don't build a blocking gate on it. Test the real timing in your own setup.

The scoring itself can take up to 30 seconds. The worker makes up to three attempts within 30 seconds of the first. It retries `5xx`, `408` and `429`, but not a timeout or any other `4xx` [S1]. If your endpoint is slow, return `503` quickly so Weave retries [S1].

**Next step:** ask your org admin to enable remote scoring and allow your scorer host. Then create the signal and run one test turn.
